protocol.name: WVAQ blind-quality selection feasibility
protocol.hypothesis: Increasing the candidate budget of a blind-IQA selector improves its selected metric score but increases active-speaker error.
protocol.design: Retrospective exploratory reuse of all 8 previously inspected UniTalk clips from 4 sources at both resolutions. Previous task outcomes known; BRISQUE selection outcomes not yet computed. No untouched-test or novelty claim.
protocol.unsharp: RGB float32: clip(round(x + amount*(x-GaussianBlur(x,sigma=1))),0,255); amounts 0.5,1,2; no other edits
protocol.primary_selector: Lowest mean BRISQUE over all 25 frames; official OpenCV 4.12.0 LIVE-R2 model; RGB converted to BGR; lexical candidate-name tie break; no labels/audio/reference access.
protocol.sampling: Exact uniform average over all candidate subsets of each size, selection of one complete clip per subset. No per-frame switching. All clips retained at 100% coverage.
protocol.primary_endpoint: Mean AV speaker error at budget4 minus budget1 (uniform random candidate); report raw-input contrast separately. Downstream original audio fixed.
secondary: error changes by source and resolution
protocol.decision: PASS only if every screening criterion holds in primary pool. PASS supports independent validation of a BRISQUE-specific failure; does not justify paper readiness, human quality claims or general IQA failure. FAIL rejects advancing this tested mechanism from these data.
protocol.statistics: Four independent source groups only; exact subset expectations and source-level effects, no frame-independent p-values; no tuning or changing gate after results.
protocol.provenance: Check all input and restoration checksums against prior receipts; check downstream A-head equality for new candidates; save per-frame IQA and downstream scores, model/code hashes, and independent arithmetic audit.
